sovereign_country.strategic_role: 最高信誉财富保护、私人银行合规与楚格州加密谷Web3枢纽

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (continental European) with cantonal administrative autonomy; company law codified in the Swiss Code of Obligations (CO/OR)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland - People's Republic of China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 27 January 2009, entered into force 6 April 2011)
Switzerland - United States Income and Capital Tax Convention (DTA) with 1996 and 2009 Protocols
Switzerland - United Kingdom DTA (signed 22 June 2016, in force 20 December 2017)
EFTA Free Trade and Economic Partnership network (30+ active FTAs applicable to Swiss entities)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG, SR 955.0 of 10 October 1997, as amended 1 January 2023); Arts. 305bis and 305ter Swiss Criminal Code; Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Persons and the Identification of their Beneficial Owners (Transparency Act, SR 221.522, adopted 22 December 2022, in force 1 July 2023); Art. 879a CO on the internal register of beneficial owners; FINMA Circular 2020/1 and FINMA AML Ordinances; SECO Financial Sanctions Regulation (Embargo Act, SR 946.231). Non-listed AG shares must be issued in registered form, and bearer shareholdings are prohibited to ensure full UBO piercing.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the certificate of incorporation / certificate of good standing of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or notarial authority of the shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for states party to the Hague Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization through the competent Swiss representation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copies of valid passports or identity documents of all natural-person UBOs and members of the Board of Directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority, evidenced by Swiss or foreign notarial certification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for foreign notarized copies; Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly signed Beneficial Owner Declaration under Art. 879a CO, including source-of-funds explanation if a PEP flag is identified
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss notary public at the incorporation deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification (domestic Swiss execution; no apostille required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney granted by foreign shareholders to the Swiss incorporation representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the shareholder's domicile state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, with certified translation into the language of the seat canton

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter evidencing a bona fide commercial relationship with the UBO/shareholder (mandatory for capital deposit documentary review at Stage 2)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of the bank officer (domestic recognition; no apostille required)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory static and continuous screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs and signatories against: (i) the SECO consolidated Swiss embargo and sanctions list; (ii) the UN Security Council consolidated list; (iii) OFAC SDN list and OFAC 50% rule logic; (iv) UK/EU consolidated sanctions lists; and (v) Swiss FDFA/MROS terrorist-financing designations. PEP classification follows AMLA Art. 2a and FINMA Circular 2020/1: any PEP or PEP-adjacent UBO triggers mandatory source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation, enhanced due diligence, and escalation to the Money Laundering Reporting Office (MROS) upon any adverse hit. Automated screening via World-Check/Refinitiv or equivalent is required before name clearance; any sanctions hit or unexplained adverse finding constitutes a blocking condition for incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Central Business Name Index (https://www.zefix.ch) and the Electronic Commercial Register interface (EHRA); registration executed through the Cantonal Commercial Register Office of the seat canton (e.g., Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Arts. 950, 954 and 956 CO and Art. 106 HRegV. The firm name must contain the legal form indicator 'AG' and may include a business designation in a Swiss federal official language (German, French, Italian or Romansh) in Latin script. An English or other foreign-language element is permissible only as a complementary, non-deceptive designation of the undertaking; Cyrillic, Chinese, Arabic or other non-Latin transliterations are not admitted as the operative legal firm name. The principle of truthfulness (Wahrheit der Firma) prohibits any misleading indication of activity, scale, or geographic scope.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Finanz / Finance / Savings (FINMA banking license required)
Insurance / Versicherung / Assurances (FINMA insurance license required)
Trust (restrictive FINMA interpretation; financial-intermediary license required for trust activity)
Investment Fund / Fonds / Fund (FINMA collective investment scheme license required)
Foundation / Stiftung / Fondation (special supervisory and capital segregation regime)
Swiss / Suisse / Schweiz / Confoederatio Helvetica (Federal Council authorization required under Art. 34a of the Coat of Arms Protection Act)
Crypto / Blockchain / Token / Payment (FINMA VASP classification and securities law assessment required)
AG / SA / Ltd / Inc / GmbH suffixes used in a misleading legal-form combination
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Preliminary name clearance is filed through the official cantonal clearance form. Upon a negative decision, the applicant may submit a written administrative appeal to the Cantonal Commercial Register supervisory authority within 30 days of receipt of the refusal; a further appeal lies to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht). A single fee-based extension of the preliminarily reserved name is available at the discretion of the Cantonal Office. Alternatively, the rejected name may be revised and resubmitted for a new clearance assessment; publication of the final name in the Federal Official Gazette (SHAB platform) is deemed the completion point of the clearance procedure.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Registered office and domiciliation services (business-centre address) are permissible for a non-licensed, non-financial e-commerce merchant (ISIC 4791), provided the registered seat is a genuine correspondence address at which legal process, the UBO register, and accounting records can be inspected, and an identifiable director or authorized administrator is reachable during official hours. A purely virtual address without physical administrative capacity or without postal access is not accepted by the Commercial Register Office and may trigger warnings under Art. 729k CO and dissolution risk for lack of substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate: 8-12% probability of an unannounced physical inspection within the first 24 months for a low-risk subscription-box merchant; risk rises to 30-40% where a virtual address is used without demonstrable operational substance, where a PEP or enhanced-CDD UBO is present, or where sanctions-relevant commodity flows are detected.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official name search and preliminary clearance for up to five proposed firm names
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal registry tariff, approx. CHF 85; statutory scale CHF 25-80 per name searched

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary name reservation and blocking entry
Notarization of the Articles of Association (Statuten) including the incorporation minute as a public deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Art. 629 and 640 CO; cantonal notary fee schedule, approx. CHF 1,200-2,200 for an AG with minimum capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cantonal Commercial Register registration fee for Aktiengesellschaft with CHF 100,000 initial capital
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal fee schedule, approx. CHF 900; statutory range CHF 600-1,200 depending on the canton

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Federal Official Gazette (SHAB) publication fee for the AG incorporation notice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Federal publication tariff, approx. CHF 125 per insertion

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO internal register preparation and Transparency Act filing setup with the Federal Office of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Federal Office of Justice and corporate services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated filing fee and preparer charge under the Transparency Act, approx. CHF 205

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / Consular Legalization bundle for one foreign corporate shareholder and UBO identification documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Apostille authority or Swiss consular representation of the document's origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial and consular tariff per document set, approx. CHF 150; excludes certified translation costs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal opinion confirming absence of a statutory license requirement for ISIC 4791 subscription-box e-commerce and AML classification
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate CHF 250-450 per hour; estimated 3-5 hours, approx. CHF 1,300

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Articles 620-659 on the Aktiengesellschaft (stock company); Articles 50-51 on articles of association; Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV), Articles 26-31 and 34; Federal Act on the Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of the registered office, with central coordination by the Federal Commercial Register Office (Fachstelle für das Handelsregister, FEDRO).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized deed of incorporation (Gründungsurkunde) and Articles of Association (Statuten), submitted electronically to the cantonal Commercial Register by a Swiss public notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital of CHF 100,000; at least 20% of the nominal value per share, and not less than CHF 20,000 in aggregate, must be paid up before registration; the funds must be held in a blocked Swiss bank account and released only upon proof of Commercial Register registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscribers, acting as the provisional Board, adopt the Articles of Association and confirm the lawful subscription of the share capital, with the minimum paid-up portion deposited in a blocked Swiss bank account. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be fixed at Zurich, Switzerland, and that the Board proceed with application to the Commercial Register Office. RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed Chairperson, [Name] Managing Director, and [Name] Secretary, each with individual or joint signatory authority, effective upon registration. RESOLVED, that the escrow release instructions be delivered to the depository bank after registration, and the Board complete all operational licensing and tax registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Escrow Capital Verification and Blocked Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a Swiss bank to open a blocked corporate account in the intended company name; deposit at least CHF 20,000 as paid-up capital; obtain banker's confirmation that funds are blocked until Commercial Register registration.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of incorporators and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises a KYC/AML query, provide enhanced source-of-funds documentation and a revised beneficial ownership declaration; re-submit until compliance clearance is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Authentication of Deed of Incorporation and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange for the public notary to authenticate the deed of incorporation, approve the Articles of Association, verify the identity of all incorporators, and certify specimen signatures of the board of directors.
required_dossiers: Passports or identity cards of all incorporators and appointed directors
Bank confirmation of blocked capital deposit
Power of attorney if a representative signs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any formal defect in the notarial deed or articles; if notarial certification is refused, amend the relevant clause and arrange a new notarial appointment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Filing and Statutory Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the registration dossier electronically to the cantonal Commercial Register; the office checks legal compliance and, upon approval, registers the company and causes publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOFC).
required_dossiers: Board resolution on officers and specimen signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice, the applicant has the statutory cure period, normally 20 days, to amend or complete the filing; failure to cure results in refusal and the filing must be resubmitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Enterprise Identification Number and Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) and Cantonal Tax Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon Commercial Register entry, the company automatically receives an enterprise identification number (UID); submit registration to the cantonal tax authority for corporate income tax, direct federal tax assessment, and withholding tax; open the tax account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is queried, provide clarification of anticipated turnover, place of effective management, and corporate purpose; adjust the submission to satisfy federal and cantonal forms.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Premises and Occupational Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Building and Commercial Police (Gewerbepolizei) and Cantonal Labour Inspectorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the municipal business notification for subscription-box warehouse or office premises, obtain fire-safety certification, structural load inspection for storage racks, and register employees with SUVA accident insurance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the premises fail inspection, cure all identified fire, egress, or loading deficiencies and submit for reinspection; secure professional corrective reports prior to re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT and Indirect Tax Election for E-Commerce Activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA), VAT Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for VAT registration if worldwide turnover from taxable supplies exceeds CHF 100,000; for subscription-box operations, confirm the tax point for periodical invoices, import VAT on inbound goods, and treatment of non-resident customers under Swiss VAT rules.
required_dossiers: Articles of Association showing business purpose
List of planned import and export activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to ESTV questions on turnover projections and mixed supplies; if VAT registration is denied for lack of economic activity, demonstrate ongoing subscription contracts and planned logistics arrangements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Cantonal Trade and Industry Office (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit / Office cantonal de l'économie et du travail); competent only for ancillary trade permits, not required for pure subscription-box retailing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required under federal or cantonal law for recurring physical subscription-box merchandising; a municipal business-premises notification (Betriebsanmeldung) and, where applicable, a cantonal warehouse operating permit may apply.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU) and the competent cantonal environmental protection agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt; under the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVP/ElE), low-impact warehousing, packaging and distribution activities for subscription boxes do not require a full EIA report; registration or a certificate may be required only when certain waste or facility thresholds are met.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Air Pollution Control Ordinance (LRV/OIAP), the Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV/LEaux), and the Clean Air Act; no significant process wastewater or VOC emissions are expected; packaging waste is subject to cantonal waste-management regulations and the Swiss Packaging Ordinance, including take-back or disposal documentation for transport packaging.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the cantonal fire prevention authority; structural load verification for racking and storage areas from a licensed engineer; workplace clearance under the Swiss Labour Code and Labour Inspection Ordinance; employees registered with SUVA (Swiss National Accident Insurance Fund).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung / Administration fédérale des contributions; ESTV/AFC), with the official e-service portal estv.admin.ch and the central UID registry at uid.admin.ch.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities apply to ESTV/AFC for Swiss VAT registration on the official form or via the secure FTA e-portal once annual taxable turnover in Switzerland exceeds CHF 250,000 or voluntary registration is chosen. The application must include: constitutive documents and current foreign company registry extract, proof of foreign tax identification, Swiss address/service address or appointed representative, sector and turnover declaration, and expected Swiss supplies. After validation, the FTA assigns the Swiss business identification number (UID/IDE/IVH) and the separate Swiss VAT number (MWST/TVA/IVA). The UID is recorded in the public UID register and is the applicable Swiss tax identification number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No United-States-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch classification election exists in Swiss federal tax law; an Aktiengesellschaft is mandatorily taxable at entity level. Relevant statutory elections affecting indirect taxation include the Swiss VAT group election (Art. 21 Federal Act on VAT) for closely integrated persons and the right to elect voluntary VAT registration below statutory thresholds.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 250,000 (for Swiss-resident businesses: annual worldwide taxable turnover; for businesses established abroad: annual turnover derived from supplies taxable in Switzerland); voluntary registration is available even below the threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, tax-authority API, or digital stamping mandate for VAT invoices. Electronic invoicing is permitted if authenticity and integrity are preserved; ordinary Swiss VAT invoice content rules apply. The Swiss QR-bill (QR-Rechnung) is introduced for machine-readable payment slips, but it is not a tax pre-clearance requirement. No invoice must be pre-approved by ESTV before issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of goods is eligible for 0% Swiss VAT if the goods are physically exported from Switzerland in the course of the taxable person's commercial activity, title passes to a foreign recipient, and the export is proven to the customs authorities, normally through a customs export declaration (e-dec Export). Offshore services supplied by a Swiss AG to a foreign recipient may be outside Swiss VAT or zero-rated under place-of-supply rules to the extent the recipient and use/benefit are abroad; the taxpayer must document the business relationship and destination. Subscription-box exports are zero-rated only when the goods leave Swiss customs territory and the shipment documentation, customer order file, and transport evidence form a complete proof chain.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhrdeklaration / déclaration en douane d'exportation) generated via e-dec Export
Bill of Lading / CMR consignment note / Air Waybill / postal dispatch certificate
Inward Remittance Certificate or Swiss-bank evidence of foreign receipt of export proceeds
Commercial invoice stating seller, buyer, destination, Incoterms and export dispatch
Subscription order/contract or ERP sales record identifying the foreign customer and delivery address
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ESTV and the Swiss Federal Customs Administration can audit export proofs and trace shipment and payment chains. If zero-rating is claimed without documentary evidence, the supply is recharacterized as taxable at the standard rate (currently 8.1%) and the input VAT deducted against the export supply is clawed back. Section 70 VATA empowers ESTV to assess tax evaded with interest; fines may reach four times the evaded VAT and criminal prosecution is possible in aggravated tax fraud cases. Ordinary limitation period is generally five to ten years depending on tax evasion or omission, with retrospective reassessment for the full limitation window.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Schweizerische Nationalbank (SNB), Bern and Zurich; administered jointly with the Federal Department of Finance. SNB is the sole monetary authority and custodian of Swiss franc (CHF) external stability, but prudential banking supervision resides with FINMA. SNB also operates the Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC/SIC4) system and enforces statistical reporting on international payments and cross-border positions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: CHF is fully convertible for current and capital account transactions. Switzerland is an IMF Article VIII member; there are no foreign exchange licensing regimes, no prior approval mandates for inward or outward transfers, and no capital controls. Profit and dividend remittance from a Swiss AG to foreign shareholders is unrestricted; the only friction is Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) of 35% on distributed dividends, which is reduced or refunded under Switzerland's extensive double taxation treaty network or domestic participation relief. The sole formal obligation is SNB statistical reporting: any resident company with aggregate foreign assets/liabilities or annual international payment flows exceeding CHF 10 million equivalent must file (or instruct its bank to file) the SNB International Payments Report; the reporting is accomplished via the banking relationship and does not constitute a convertibility barrier.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Swiss law imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation timeline, or conversion ratio for export proceeds. A Swiss AG may freely retain export receivables in USD, EUR, CNY, or other currencies, hold them in foreign-currency accounts, and convert at market rates or execute hedges without SNB approval. For the subscription-box business, cross-border card settlement flows are credited in original currency to the operational account and may be swept to CHF at the company's discretion. The only ancillary duty is accurate declaration of goods in Swiss Customs (e-dec/eTAS) and correct payment-purpose labelling for SNB statistics; no statutory deadline for conversion exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.fnma_aml_insight_note: Not part of the schema but relevant: FINMA Circular 2018/8 and Swiss AMLA (SR 955.0) require banks to validate the economic background of every transaction and the identity of the UBO; the subscription-box model must therefore maintain a complete audit trail of merchant settlements and supplier invoices.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Sperrkonto) plus Multi-Currency Operational Treasury Account (CHF/EUR/USD/CNY)
Capital Escrow Account plus Operational Account with SEPA, SIC4 Instant Payments, and e-commerce settlement rails
Operational Account and Card-Acquiring Settlement Account
Operational Account for domestic CHF treasury, payroll, and supplier payments
Wealth-linked liquidity and investment account; not suited as primary transactional rail

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: MEDIUM-HIGH as an ancillary card-collection or multi-currency settlement node; LOW as the primary treasury institution. Foreign digital EMIs (Wise Business, Revolut Business, Airwallex, Paysera) are not FINMA-licensed banks and may not lawfully accept deposits from the Swiss public under Art. 1 Banking Act. They operate under UK EMI or EU PSD2 licences, typically holding client funds in pooled safeguarding accounts at partner banks rather than segregated Swiss bank accounts. For a subscription-box AG, an EMI may be used for customer card settlement and cross-border supplier payouts, provided: (i) the EMI is fully licensed in its home EEA/UK jurisdiction, (ii) the company's principal operating account and statutory capital deposit remain at a FINMA-regulated bank, and (iii) balances are swept daily to the Swiss account to avoid unlicensed deposit exposure and opaque payment-purpose classification. EMIs may not be used for payroll, Swiss tax, or share-capital escrow.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory for at least one managing director. Swiss banks rarely offer remote opening for AG clients with foreign shareholders; prevailing market practice requires an in-person interview at a Swiss branch or at a Swiss embassy/consulate with notarisation of the director's identity and signature specimen. FINMA Circular 2018/8 permits video-based identification only where the bank operates an FINMA-accredited online identity solution, but for a cross-border e-commerce entity most compliance officers still demand a physical economic-background discussion covering the subscription-box model, target markets, expected payment volumes, marketing channels, and the ultimate beneficial owner chain. The onboarding blueprint must therefore assume at least one physical visit to Switzerland, plus apostilled corporate documents and original passport verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border retail subscription traffic with fractional recurring charge amounts (CHF 5–CHF 50) and elevated refund/chargeback velocity, which banks may profile as mule-account or layering activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) merchant statements from Stripe Billing and Authorize.Net/Braintree evidencing recurring transaction patterns, (ii) PCI-DSS Level 1 attestation of compliance, (iii) publicly accessible e-commerce website with terms and conditions, privacy policy, and refund/cancellation policy, (iv) monthly settlement ledgers mapping each card transaction to fulfilment records, (v) historical chargeback ratio report demonstrating a dispute rate below 0.5%, and (vi) a written narrative of the subscription-box commercial model, sourcing strategy, and customer acquisition channels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity caused by holding-company shareholders in low-tax jurisdictions or nominee structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Swiss Commercial Register extract (Handelsregisterauszug), notarised UBO declaration under Art. 9 AMLA, certified passport copies of all natural-person ultimate owners, a signed group structure chart with ownership percentages, audited or reviewed financial statements of the parent entity, and a bank statement evidencing the source of the share-capital deposit to be wired from the declared shareholder's own account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume third-party payment settlement into the corporate account from payment processors instead of direct identifiable customers, potentially implicating the bank in unlicensed payment intermediation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial agreements with Stripe Inc. and Authorize.Net, merchant ID documentation, daily settlement report samples, a reconciliation statement linking SWIFT reference tags to transaction IDs, an explanation of chargeback reserves held by the processor, and a compliance declaration that the company exclusively uses FINMA-compliant or EU-heavyweight processors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Supply-chain exposure to elevated-risk manufacturing jurisdictions (China, Hong Kong, Turkey, India), raising trade-based money-laundering concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier KYB files (business licences), pro forma invoices and purchase orders for each sourcing batch, Incoterms clauses in purchase contracts, Swiss Customs e-dec/eTAS export and import declarations, carrier bills of lading, and a sanctions-screening policy demonstrating that neither the AG nor its counterparties transact with sanctioned entities.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Statutory share capital (minimum CHF 100,000 total, with at least CHF 50,000 paid in at incorporation) is routed via SWIFT MT103/ISO 20022 from the shareholder's overseas bank using purpose code 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION / SUBSCRIPTION FOR SHARES' and referencing the notarial deed and the pending Commercial Register filing. The receiving Swiss bank credits the funds to a blocked capital escrow account (Sperrkonto); release occurs only upon registration of the AG in the Commercial Register. For a subsequent capital increase, the same protocol applies with reference to the notarial capital-increase deed and shareholder resolution. EUR contributions from EEA shareholders may use SEPA Credit Transfer; all other inbound flows must be SWIFT. Each inward transfer above CHF 15,000 triggers an automatic request for source-of-funds documentation; the mandatory rule is that funds must originate from the declared shareholder's own account and never from a third party, otherwise the deposit may be treated as unlicensed public deposit-taking or trigger an AML investigation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA suppliers and international freight, with purpose code 'TRADE PAYMENT / PURCHASE OF GOODS' and reference to the commercial invoice; (2) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for EU/EEA suppliers in EUR; (3) SIC4 instant CHF payments for domestic logistics, payroll, and recurring Swiss-service invoices; (4) Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600) and documentary collections (URC 522) for high-value inventory sourcing above USD 100,000, quoted via a Swiss confirming bank with a cash margin of typically 10–30%. Each outward disbursement must be matched with the underlying supplier invoice, customs declaration, and proof of delivery to satisfy FINMA AML audit and SNB statistical reporting; no pre-approval from FINMA or SNB is required for outbound wires. For subscription-box customer refunds, use the card-processor reversal rail first; bank-level wires are reserved for B2B or regulatory refunds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (USD/CHF, EUR/CHF, CNY/CHF) with tenors up to 12 months under ISDA or a Swiss Master Agreement, available from UBS, ZKB, and BCV without SNB approval
FX Swaps (near-leg/far-leg) for rolling the currency mismatch between card-settlement USD balances and CHF operational liquidity
European-style vanilla FX Options (calls and puts) and zero-premium option collars to protect the EBIT margin of subscription-box revenue against EUR/USD and CHF appreciation
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) to hedge long-term mismatches between foreign-currency cash holdings and CHF-denominated borrowings
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on exotic sourcing currencies (TRY, INR, IDR) where onshore deliverability is restricted; NDFs on CHF are unnecessary because CHF is fully convertible
OTC FX limit-order sweeps for daily conversion of customer card settlement balances into CHF at best execution, executed via the bank's e-banking treasury module

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) notice, minutes and shareholder resolutions approving the annual financial statements and granting discharge to the Board of Directors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not filed externally; kept in the corporate records and made available to shareholders, auditors, tax authorities, and judicial authorities upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of the fiscal year; for calendar-year company by 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM is an offence under Art. 731 of the Swiss Code of Obligations; may trigger a court-appointed examiner upon shareholder petition and continued non-compliance can lead to directors' liability; no automatic government fine for private companies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (federal, cantonal and communal) with financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, notes and management report) and any required audit evidence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) in Bern and competent Cantonal Tax Administration (for registered office, e.g., Canton Zug Tax Office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Usually within 30 days after the tax authority issues the fiscal assessment form; typical deadlines range from March to November of the year following the tax year; extensions available on written request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 4% per annum on unpaid assessed tax; late filing penalties up to 25% of the assessed tax; deliberate non-filing constitutes tax evasion subject to fines up to CHF 250,000 and imprisonment up to three years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Swiss VAT annual return (VAT declaration including subscription sales and input VAT) for taxpayers using the annual reporting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) – Swiss VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by 30 April of the year following the reporting year for annual return filers; quarterly returns are due within 60 days after the end of each quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission surcharge of up to 3% of the VAT amount owed; default interest of 3.5% per annum; continued failure may trigger a penal assessment and loss of deduction entitlements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: AHV annual wage report and social security contribution declaration for employees (Beitragsnachweis) including subscription box operations payroll data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Social Insurance Office (BSV) and the competent AHV compensation fund
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March following the end of the calendar year for the prior year's payroll; monthly/quarterly interim payments are due on schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Arrears interest of 5% per annum on unpaid employer and employee contributions; civil fines for incomplete submissions; criminal prosecution for fraudulent non-declaration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Register notifications and statutory disclosures (share capital changes, director updates, registered office moves) – event-driven, not an annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) and Swiss Commercial Register (SHAB publication)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days of any reportable event; for changes in the register of beneficial owners, within 30 days of a relevant beneficial ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration penalties up to CHF 200 per day; continued omissions can lead to a court order to file and may cause the company to lose legal standing or incur criminal liability under commercial register law.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Full statutory audit (Ordentliche Revision) is mandatory if the company exceeds two of the three following thresholds in two consecutive fiscal years: total assets CHF 20 million, annual turnover CHF 40 million, or 250 average full-time employees; also mandatory for Swiss companies with listed equity or debt. Await; if the company does not meet these thresholds, a limited audit (Zweckmässige Revision) is required unless shareholders unanimously decide to waive any audit because the company, on average over one year, does not exceed 10 full-time employees.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations (Art. 957–958e) commercial accounting requirements; larger entities may elect Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS; for subscription-based revenue, IFRS 15 / Swiss GAAP FER revenue recognition rules apply to deferred income and subscriber contract balances.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law does not impose an annual UBO confirmation filing. The federal Transparency Register under the Beneficial Owners Ordinance (VOBen) is event-triggered: initial registration within 60 days of incorporation or commercial register entry, and any change in beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days. For an Aktiengesellschaft, the share register (Aktienregister) must be maintained continuously to record transfers; the commercial register must be updated for director and statutory auditor changes within 14 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Statutory Auditors
Minutes of General Meetings and Board Resolutions (Minute Book)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 10,000 per year for a limited audit; USD 15,000 - 30,000 for a full statutory audit depending on entity size and complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal direct corporate income tax on post-tax profit (equivalent to 7.83% pre-tax) plus cantonal/communal corporate tax; combined effective headline in Zug, the reference Web3 jurisdiction, ≈ 11.9% to 14.9%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Patent/IP box: 90% exemption of qualified IP income; R&D super-deduction up to 150% of qualifying R&D labour costs (Zug); notional interest deduction (NID) on excess capital up to CHF 1 million or goodwill; participation exemption of 100% on qualifying dividend and capital gains (≥10% participation); no capital tax for low-tax profile companies? Actually, there is a cantonal capital tax that can be reduced; new companies in certain cantons get capital tax reductions.
